Question: If \(x\) is real and positive and grows beyond all bounds, then \(\log_3(6x-5)-\log_3(2x+1)\) approaches:
Solution:
The two logarithms have the same base, so combining them lets us compare their arguments directly. For sufficiently large \(x\), we have \(x>5/6\), ensuring that both arguments are positive. The quotient rule gives
\[
\log_3(6x-5)-\log_3(2x+1)
=\log_3\left(\frac{6x-5}{2x+1}\right).
\]
Rewrite the fraction to separate its constant part:
\[
\frac{6x-5}{2x+1}
=3-\frac8{2x+1}.
\]
As \(x\) grows beyond all bounds, \(8/(2x+1)\) approaches zero, so this positive argument approaches \(3\). The logarithmic function is continuous at the positive input \(3\), hence the expression approaches \(\log_3 3=1\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
